hero.headline: Applications open for free and reduced-price school meals in Indian River County
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility for free or reduced-price school meals.

Families need their child's Student ID number and full formal name as listed in FOCUS. They also need a valid email address and either internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Households receiving Florida Medicaid benefits should have their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. This is the Medicaid case number, not the Medicaid card number. The case number can be found by logging into MyACCESS or looking at the Notice of Eligibility Review letter from the Florida Department of Children and Families. The case number is printed at the top of the letter.

To apply, families visit www.LINQConnect.com and either sign in or create an account. New users can click Register to create a free account. Families then search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their students by entering the Student ID and using the formal name as listed in FOCUS, not nicknames. From the website homepage, families click School Services at the top menu and then select Free and Reduced Meal Application. Families using the app go to the homepage and click Free and Reduced Meal Application under Quick Links. Applicants fill in household information and income details and submit the application. Families receive an email when the application is processed.

Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.

cards.headline: Second arrest made in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced Tuesday that a second person has been arrested in the fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes, 66. Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. Deputies said the fatal shooting was premeditated.

The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Karen Moye was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes.

Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, is now facing charges for false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Tuesday during a press conference that detectives uncovered information indicating Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. Moye told detectives immediately after the shooting that Mincey and Barnes did not have a good relationship and that Mincey expressed fear in the days leading up to the shooting. Moye said Mincey told her Barnes was trying to kill him and Mincey did not want to be left alone at the house. In a follow-up interview on Monday, Moye gave a detective conflicting accounts of what happened on the day of the shooting. She told detectives she was in fear of Barnes and that something might happen between Mincey and Barnes. When asked why she didn't notify police, she said she thought both of them would get in trouble. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, though he admitted to owning two firearms.

Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as a pillar of the community and a father figure. The fatal shooting remains an active investigation. Deputies are encouraging anyone with information that has yet to be shared with investigators to contact the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, or to remain anonymous contact the Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Man fleeing ICE agents struck and killed by truck on Florida State Road 16
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after being struck by a semi trailer truck while fleeing from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents on State Road 16 in Florida. The man was one of four people who ran from the scene during an encounter with ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents in the parking lot of a local gas station and convenience store, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The man ran across State Road 16 and into the path of the tractor trailer. He was struck in the right lane and sustained fatal injuries on scene, according to a statement from the Florida Highway Patrol. The agency confirmed it was not involved in the incident but has since opened an investigation into the death. Details about the victim, including their name, nationality and immigration status, were not immediately available. The three other individuals who fled have not been located or identified by authorities.

ICE and the Department of Homeland Security have not yet commented on the incident. The death comes as ICE faces increasing scrutiny for multiple fatal encounters. On Monday, Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man living in Maine, was fatally shot by ICE agents during a traffic stop. Senator Angus King said Guerrero was not the target of an immigration operation. Days earlier, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally wounded during a traffic stop involving ICE in Houston. Like the shooting in Maine, Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was trying to find.

The Trump administration ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to pause most traffic stops on Tuesday following the deadly incidents. Florida Highway Patrol officials continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death on State Road 16. The incident remains under investigation and is being treated as a developing story.

cards.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap over next 20 years
cards.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall that could shape how residents get around for decades. A PowerPoint obtained through a public records request shows the Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years. Only $701 million is currently available, meaning the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August, outlining transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories through 2050. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources.

The funding gap leaves nine roads requiring widening unfunded, at a total cost of approximately $213 million. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. May and Maddy Brumlow travel Martin Downs Boulevard nearly every day and said the congestion is already noticeable. Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said funding shortfalls of this scale are not unusual. State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities due to safety concerns. Residents can submit input to the Martin County MPO by contacting Principal Planner Ricardo Vazquez at rvazquez@martin.fl.us or by calling (772) 223-7983.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents pack planning meeting over 17-story Causeway Cove high-rise proposal
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project on Monday as neighbors packed the chamber. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space. The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. "We're going to put this big old conglomerate up here, and I'm just afraid it's going to take away from the beauty of this place," Brewster said. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic. "Nobody's thought this out. You're going to have massive traffic jams. Nobody's going to be able to get on the island, off the island," Fein said. City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved. "The city does not have a play here. We do not have a position in this. This is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. The city has been eliminated from the process," Broderick said. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Florida Democrats cite special election wins as evidence of possible legislative comeback in 2026
cards.teaser: Florida Democrats say recent special election victories and increased volunteer activity show the Republican supermajority in the state Legislature is breakable, though the party still faces a voter registration deficit of more than 1.5 million.
cards.body:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said Monday the Republican supermajority in the Legislature is breakable, outlining a path she says could move the state's politics back toward the middle after decisive statewide losses in 2022 and 2024. During a virtual briefing, the party pointed to more than 30 local and special-election flips since the 2024 election, more than 3,000 volunteers, increased candidate recruitment and an advantage in requests for vote-by-mail ballots. The party's tally includes local offices as well as recent legislative special elections, not 30 seats in the Florida Legislature. Fried attributed the progress to the party's Pendulum Project, a year-round organizing operation designed to maintain voter contact between major elections.

Democrats are building their message around affordability, blaming nearly three decades of Republican control for rising housing, property insurance, healthcare and everyday living costs. Fried said candidates will challenge a Republican-backed property tax amendment headed to voters, arguing that cutting local government revenue could threaten services or shift costs elsewhere. Republicans have built a voter registration advantage of more than 1.5 million. As of May 31, Florida had about 5.54 million active registered Republicans and 4.03 million Democrats, according to the state Division of Elections. Another 3.32 million voters were registered without a party affiliation. Republicans remain at or above the two-thirds threshold needed for supermajority power in both legislative chambers.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
hero.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as Dave Motz battles head and neck cancer. The couple has faced nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket medical costs while traveling to Orlando for daily radiation treatments.
hero.body:
Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis just months after purchasing property and settling in the area. The couple met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised three children. Faren home schooled all three kids while the family ran a farm that served children. After Dave, a former firefighter, was diagnosed with head and neck cancer, the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida. AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments, and the repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams cost the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

Doctors told Dave he has an 85 percent chance of recovery. Dave had long been the family's provider, but Faren has now stepped up to support them both, driving him back and forth from Orlando for treatment. The couple has leaned on their faith throughout the experience. Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Pickup truck fire closes lane on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded Monday morning to a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck fire on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175.
cards.body: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a vehicle fire Monday morning on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175. Firefighters arrived to find a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck on the shoulder of the interstate. Crews initiated an aggressive fire attack, bringing the fire under control while working alongside the Florida Highway Patrol to maintain a safe scene for motorists. Traffic was temporarily impacted as firefighters extinguished the fire and secured the scene. No additional vehicles were involved. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November, 6,000-seat venue at Walton & One development
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat stadium at the Walton & One development on U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Groundbreaking is anticipated in November with current plans targeting a 2028 opening.
hero.body:
Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction.

The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. Calling it a year-round gathering place, the club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity. The team also said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League League One Team. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. Focus Sanders, a barber at Sapp's Barbershop, said the development offers more business because it will bring more people to the area.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council to vote on commercial rezoning near Tradition despite neighbor concerns
cards.teaser: A proposal to change nearly 9.5 acres near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive from residential to commercial use is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before Port St. Lucie City Council Monday.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of the nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The proposal, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from a residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. The city says the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, but any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes.

The Mucciolos told Port St. Lucie City Council two months ago they feared changing the land from residential to commercial could alter the character of the community. This is our backyard. This is where we spend the majority of our day, Joseph Mucciolo said. It's going to be gone, and if they put up a wall it's going to look like a prison. The family says they worry losing the open space behind their home could impact the quality of life they value.

The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May. Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive.

hero.headline: World Cup semifinals set as England and Argentina advance to final four
hero.teaser: England's Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway, while Argentina's Julin Alvarez scored in extra time to help the team past Switzerland.
hero.body:
We were treated to two brilliant quarterfinals over the weekend, which saw both England and Argentina advance to the last four at the expense of Norway and Switzerland. For England, Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. The 23-year-old has scored six goals in the competition. Argentina has Julián Alvarez to thank after the striker scored an absolute worldie in extra time to help the team through to the semifinal, with a little help from a controversial VAR call. The last four is now complete with the four highest-ranked teams reaching the semifinals.

Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition, and England would have been knocked out much earlier if it didn't have these two superstars to rely on. England was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018 but lost on that occasion to Croatia. Argentina is the defending champion and has also relied on moments of brilliance to sneak through the knockout rounds, flirting with elimination on more than one occasion. Argentina has scored the most goals out of anyone in the competition with 17. Many members of the current squad won the title back in 2022. France will face Spain in the other semifinal on Tuesday. Considered by many to be the tournament favorite, France has barely gotten out of first gear so far this summer. Kylian Mbappé has been superb yet again, with his pace and directness proving highly effective. Spain beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024 and also beat Les Bleus in the Nations League last year. The final will be held on July 19.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner wins second straight Wimbledon title, defeating Alexander Zverev
cards.teaser: The top-ranked tennis player beat Alexander Zverev in four sets Sunday after his German opponent appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip to the grass.
cards.body:
Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 Sunday for his second consecutive title at Wimbledon after Zverev appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip to the grass on a key point in the third set. Sinner's fifth Grand Slam title came in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, the Italian dropped to the grass on his back in celebration.

A year ago, Sinner beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final at the All England Club after wasting three match points against his rival in the Roland Garros final. It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Linda Noskova beat Karolina Muchova in an all-Czech women's final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam title.

The top two seeds appeared perfectly matched until Zverev earned his first break point of the match at 3-3 in the third set, two hours and 42 minutes in. Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Despite the defeat in the final, Zverev will leapfrog Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon after recovering from five blown match points
cards.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player recovered from a second-set meltdown to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final Saturday.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova is the latest in a long line of Czech women to win Wimbledon. The 21-year-old Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was the greatest Czech-born player of them all, Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS to headline World Cup final halftime show
cards.teaser: The 11-minute halftime performance will take place during the final outside New York on July 19, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin.
cards.body:
Justin Bieber will bring his swag to the World Cup's star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show, joining fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer. Bieber said in a statement that he is grateful to be part of the halftime show and even more grateful knowing it is already helping expand access to education for children around the world.

The addition of Burna Boy is particularly noteworthy because he is one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of their musical landscapes, Afrobeats and Latin rhythms, an undeniably global, multilingual pop track. In one verse, they name several of the world's most famous soccer players and countries competing in this year's World Cup, including Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia, Mexico, Japan, Korea and Netherlands. While the Super Bowl is famed for its halftime show, such performances are not commonplace in soccer, with events like the Champions League final featuring a pre-match concert. This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 6,000-seat soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November at Walton & One
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat soccer stadium, with representatives announcing Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated for November at the Walton & One development. The 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project is located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said he thinks there's nothing to do in PSL for the most part and this may be the first cool thing they've ever actually brought here. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The club said on X that every space has been designed to create unforgettable experiences, from matchdays to concerts, festivals, and community events, calling it a destination built for everyone.

Businesses like Sapp's Barbershop say it's a chance to profit off added foot traffic. Barber Focus Sanders said it offers more business because it's going to bring more people over here, with people coming from maybe out of town who didn't get a haircut. Woods said you can't really even get out here on US-1 before this, calling it a nightmare, and he thinks the additional traffic on gamedays will be huge. Sanders said he is not liking the traffic that's going to come but is liking the business traffic. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League (USL) League One Team. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. The team said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online.

hero.headline: Man fleeing ICE agents struck and killed by truck on Florida State Road 16
hero.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after being struck by a semi trailer truck while fleeing from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents on State Road 16 in Florida. The man was one of four people who ran from the scene during an encounter with ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents in the parking lot of a local gas station and convenience store, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The man ran across State Road 16 and into the path of the tractor trailer. He was struck in the right lane and sustained fatal injuries on scene, according to a statement from the Florida Highway Patrol. The agency confirmed it was not involved in the incident but has since opened an investigation into the death. Details about the victim, including their name, nationality and immigration status, were not immediately available. The three other individuals who fled have not been located or identified by authorities.

ICE and the Department of Homeland Security have not yet commented on the incident. The death comes as ICE faces increasing scrutiny for multiple fatal encounters. On Monday, Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man living in Maine, was fatally shot by ICE agents during a traffic stop. Senator Angus King said Guerrero was not the target of an immigration operation. Days earlier, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally wounded during a traffic stop involving ICE in Houston. Like the shooting in Maine, Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was trying to find.

The Trump administration ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to pause most traffic stops on Tuesday following the deadly incidents. Florida Highway Patrol officials continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death on State Road 16. The incident remains under investigation and is being treated as a developing story.

cards.headline: Three lawsuits challenge Florida property tax amendment ballot language before November vote
cards.teaser: A Republican-backed property tax amendment headed to Florida voters in November faces three separate legal challenges over whether the ballot language fairly explains the measure or amounts to a political sales pitch.
cards.body:
Three separate lawsuits now challenge Amendment Three, a proposed constitutional amendment placed on the November ballot by state lawmakers. The legal challenges have been filed by nonprofit Save Our Voters, former South Miami Mayor Philip Stoddard, and former lawmakers Jeff Brandes and Al Lawson. All three cases make the same core argument: the ballot language is biased, misleading and written to persuade voters rather than neutrally explain the amendment. Attorney Jamie Cole, who filed the first lawsuit, said the language is as biased as bias can be and called it basically a political flyer. The lawsuits target several phrases in the ballot summary, including language saying the amendment would save homes from excessive property taxes, protect small businesses, ensure funding for core services and ensure fairness for Florida residents. Plaintiffs argue those phrases are campaign-style language urging voters to support the measure rather than a neutral explanation of what the amendment does.

The cases are expected to be consolidated, with a hearing currently set for July 29. If approved by 60 percent of voters, the measure would expand non-school homestead property tax exemptions, eventually exempting up to $250,000 of a homestead's value by 2028. It would also limit some future assessment increases on non-homestead property and place new restrictions on how local governments use property tax dollars. If a judge agrees the ballot language is misleading, the Florida Attorney General could be tasked with rewriting the summary. The amendment needs at least 60 percent voter approval to pass in November.

cards.headline: Florida Democrats cite special election wins as evidence of possible legislative comeback in 2026
cards.teaser: Florida Democrats say recent special election victories and increased volunteer activity show the Republican supermajority in the state Legislature is breakable, though the party still faces a voter registration deficit of more than 1.5 million.
cards.body:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said Monday the Republican supermajority in the Legislature is breakable, outlining a path she says could move the state's politics back toward the middle after decisive statewide losses in 2022 and 2024. During a virtual briefing, the party pointed to more than 30 local and special-election flips since the 2024 election, more than 3,000 volunteers, increased candidate recruitment and an advantage in requests for vote-by-mail ballots. The party's tally includes local offices as well as recent legislative special elections, not 30 seats in the Florida Legislature. Fried attributed the progress to the party's Pendulum Project, a year-round organizing operation designed to maintain voter contact between major elections.

Democrats are building their message around affordability, blaming nearly three decades of Republican control for rising housing, property insurance, healthcare and everyday living costs. Fried said candidates will challenge a Republican-backed property tax amendment headed to voters, arguing that cutting local government revenue could threaten services or shift costs elsewhere. Republicans have built a voter registration advantage of more than 1.5 million. As of May 31, Florida had about 5.54 million active registered Republicans and 4.03 million Democrats, according to the state Division of Elections. Another 3.32 million voters were registered without a party affiliation. Republicans remain at or above the two-thirds threshold needed for supermajority power in both legislative chambers.

cards.headline: Rising home insurance costs driving Florida voter turnout ahead of 2026 midterms, study finds
cards.teaser: A new study shows 65 percent of Florida respondents say rising insurance costs are making them more likely to vote in the 2026 midterm elections, higher than the national average of 58 percent.
cards.body:
The cost of homeowners insurance is becoming a key political issue ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, according to a new study from online insurance marketplace Insurify. The study found 65 percent of Florida respondents said rising insurance costs would make them more likely to vote in the 2026 midterms, compared to 58 percent of Americans nationally. Insurify puts the Florida statewide average premium at $8,292, with a modest 2 percent increase expected this year. Insurify economist Julia Taliesin said the study examined whether there was any connection in some states between the political environment and insurance regulation.

The study also found 84 percent of Florida respondents plan to vote in the 2026 midterms, with 72 percent of Florida respondents identifying as homeowners. Forty-nine percent of Florida homeowners reported their home insurance premiums increased in the last 12 months. Fifty-seven percent of Florida respondents feel negative about the state of the economy, and 71 percent of Florida respondents believe elections affect home insurance costs in their state. According to state leaders, reforms on insurance litigation have led to stable and in many cases lower rates as more companies enter Florida adding to competition. Yet in many parts of the state, including South Florida, insurance premiums have risen as inflation and home values have increased. Republican state leaders this year have been leading the charge for property tax reform as a new affordability target.

cards.headline: Judge sets July 21 hearing on lawsuit challenging James Fishback residency in Florida governor's race
cards.teaser: A Leon County judge scheduled a two-day hearing for July 21 and 22 to decide whether Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement to run for governor.
cards.body:
A Leon County judge has set aside two days later this month to decide whether James Fishback can remain on the Republican ballot for Florida governor. During a Tuesday scheduling hearing, Judge David Frank set the matter for July 21 and 22, warning attorneys there is an extreme shortage of time with the Aug. 18 primary approaching. Frank noted it is likely already too late to stop ballots from being printed, saying there would need to be an injunction to the Department of State telling supervisors of elections not to count the votes and to post a notice. The lawsuit was filed by Lt. Governor Jay Collins, one of Fishback's rivals in the GOP primary. Collins argues Fishback does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement to run for governor, with his complaint pointing to records tied to Fishback's voter registration and residency in Washington, D.C.

Fishback's attorney, former state representative Anthony Sabatini, told the judge the case turns on more than paperwork, arguing Fishback's intent will be central to determining residency. Sabatini said the defense wants time to present witnesses and documents. The courtroom fight comes just days after the issue spilled onto the debate stage during last week's GOP primary debate, where Fishback, Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner appeared together. Fishback pressed Collins directly over the lawsuit and later accused Collins of trying to steal the election with Byron Donalds. Collins pushed back, saying the challenge belongs in court and that he respects the judicial system. Frontrunner Byron Donalds skipped the debate but continues to maintain a commanding position in the primary through polling, fundraising and endorsements. Witness and exhibit lists are due five days before the July 21 hearing.

cards.headline: Former Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum arrested on drug charges in Alabama
cards.teaser: Former Tallahassee mayor and 2018 Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum was arrested July 2 in Daphne, Alabama, on marijuana and methamphetamine possession charges after police stopped him for erratic driving.
cards.body:
Gillum, 46, was arrested on July 2 in Daphne, about 11 miles east of Mobile on Alabama's Gulf Coast. He is charged with marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a controlled substance, the Daphne Police Department said. Jail records show he was released on July 3. In a news release, the Daphne Police Department said officers stopped Gillum's vehicle around 10:45 p.m. and initiated a probable cause search after one of them noticed a glass pipe on the center console. They found several rolled marijuana cigarettes and three packages of a substance that tested positive for methamphetamine, police said.

Gillum served as mayor of Florida's capital from 2014 to 2018 and came within less than a percentage point of being elected the state's first Black governor, losing to Ron DeSantis by fewer than 34,000 votes. In 2020, Gillum was found in a Miami Beach hotel room with a man who had apparently overdosed on drugs. Police said Gillum himself was too inebriated to talk about what happened. The man survived and no one was ever charged with a crime for the overdose. Gillum withdrew from public life for months afterward while seeking treatment for alcohol abuse and depression. In 2022, Gillum was indicted on federal conspiracy and wire fraud charges for allegedly funneling tens of thousands of dollars in campaign donations through third parties back to himself for personal use. A 2023 trial ended in a hung jury on those charges and an acquittal on charges that Gillum lied to undercover FBI agents. Gillum is a co-host of the politically themed Native Land Pod, which won the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding News and Information Podcast in 2025.

cards.headline: Florida's annual Python Challenge begins with $10,000 prize for invasive snake removal
cards.teaser: The 10-day Florida Python Challenge runs from July 10 through July 19, offering hunters a $10,000 grand prize for removing the most invasive Burmese pythons from the Everglades ecosystem.
cards.body:
The state's annual Florida Python Challenge began Friday with hunters seeking to nab snakes and big prize money. The 10-day challenge, held from July 10-19, 2026, aims to raise awareness about invasive Burmese pythons, support community involvement and help protect the Everglades ecosystem. The event first began in 2013 as Florida works to contain the invasive species, which was introduced to the area through the pet trade decades ago. State wildlife officials say the snakes pose a significant threat since there are few predators and they frequently prey upon native wildlife. The first-place hunter participating in the challenge nets a $10,000 grand prize. Organizers say registration for this year's hunt will remain open through the final day of the challenge.

Last year's hunt resulted in a record removal of 294 invasive Burmese pythons, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. The Ultimate Grand Prize of $10,000 was awarded to Taylor Stanberry for removing 60 pythons. Anyone may remove and humanely kill pythons and other nonnative reptiles at any time on private lands with landowner permission and on 32 FWC-managed lands throughout South Florida, according to FWC. The U.S. Geological Survey says on its website it is very difficult to estimate how many Burmese pythons are living in South Florida, but conservatively, tens of thousands of invasive Burmese pythons are estimated to be present in the Greater Everglades region.

hero.headline: Martin County brush fires contained after lightning strike, but more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said this is their peak season for brush fires. The summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them receptive and ready to ignite when lightning strikes occur. Grubitch explained that rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later.

Grubitch said the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. He stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire. If you see something, say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as Dave battles head and neck cancer, facing nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket medical costs from radiation treatments at AdventHealth in Celebration.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. The couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida before AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up to nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both. Doctors told Dave he has an 85 percent chance of recovery. Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as shoppers look for ways to cut grocery costs
cards.teaser: A new Aldi located at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road opened Thursday in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers facing tight budgets as grocery prices continue to rise.
cards.body:
Customers like Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. The store, located at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road, opened Thursday. Cheryl Cooperman said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. She said they are the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what is on sale instead of just with what they want.

The opening of the store in Martin County comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8 percent this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1 percent. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3 percent from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1 percent from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3 percent over the same period. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon, saying prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness holds fundraiser for family of 5-year-old killed in bike accident
cards.teaser: A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is raising funds for the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old boy who was killed when he was hit by a pickup truck while riding a bicycle at a motocross park in Miami.
cards.body:
A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is raising funds for the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old boy who was killed in an accident. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says Garrett was riding a bicycle in between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami and was hit when he crossed the path of a pickup truck. MDSO says the driver cooperated in the investigation and told them on Wednesday that no charges had been filed in the case.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier and gym owner Tabitha Lavery learned of the tragedy that struck two of their members and organized a fundraiser workout. Collier described Garrett's father as showing great pride in his son, saying he would share "This is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad." Lavery described the couple as valued members of the community and said they put together a 90-minute fundraiser workout to help the family get through this hard time. The workout is this Sunday and is open to the public. All of the proceeds will go toward a GoFundMe started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one.

cards.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
cards.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall that could shape how residents get around for decades. A PowerPoint obtained through a public records request shows the Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years. Only $701 million is currently available, meaning the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories through 2050. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources.

Nine roads the county identified as requiring widening to handle growing traffic remain unfunded. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. The roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. May and Maddy Brumlow travel Martin Downs Boulevard nearly every day and said the congestion is already noticeable. Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities due to fatal crashes and serious injury crashes, with improvements totaling about $300 million.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
hero.teaser: The Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project Monday, which includes five high-rise buildings with one 17-story building standing 192 feet tall and more than 900 apartments and condos.
hero.body:
The Causeway Cove development project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing. The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years.

Neighbors packed the chamber Monday as the Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the plans. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area and take away from the beauty of the place. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody thought this out and there will be massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island. City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the project is regulated by the state of Florida in its entirety and the city has been eliminated from the process. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind their home, says voices went unheard
cards.teaser: Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo opposed the Port St. Lucie City Council's unanimous vote to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, a change they fought for months.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously to rezone the lot behind the Mucciolo home from residential to commercial, despite the couple's months-long opposition. Margaret Mucciolo said the beautiful setting drew them to the property, telling her real estate agent to get ready to make an offer because it felt like home. Their backyard, the views of nature, and a sense of quiet relaxation pushed them to purchase. Joseph Mucciolo said in six months or a year the trees behind their yard are going to be gone. The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood, with one council member explaining that adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because trips are shorter and it reduces the burden on the overall network.

The couple spoke at Monday's meeting voicing their concerns, but they feel the council left them unheard. Joseph Mucciolo asked where they go from here and whether they can make an objection and have this looked at again. The council held its second reading Monday, and while there was public comment, it was a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion. Margaret Mucciolo said the process needs to change until it is logical, transparent, caring, and provides hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie neighbors express concerns over commercial rezoning near Tradition
cards.teaser: Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive that is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before city council Monday.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from a residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. The city says the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, but any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. The proposal is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before Port St. Lucie City Council Monday.

The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May. Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. Joseph Mucciolo said if they put up a wall it's going to look like a prison. The family says they worry losing the open space behind their home could impact the quality of life they value. Margaret Mucciolo said they do not want over development. Joseph Mucciolo said if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's 6,000-seat soccer stadium groundbreaking planned for November
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat stadium to be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road.
cards.body:
Groundbreaking for Port St. Lucie SC's 6,000-seat stadium is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said there is nothing to do in PSL for the most part and this may be the first cool thing the city has ever actually brought here.

The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. Calling it a year-round gathering place, the club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity. Barber Focus Sanders from Sapp's Barbershop said it offers more business because it's going to bring more people over here from maybe out of town who didn't get a haircut. Woods said you can't really even get out on U.S. 1 before this and it's a nightmare, so the additional traffic on gamedays will be huge. The team said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League League One Team. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen named Southeast Region Youth of the Year surprised with FIFA World Cup finals trip
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz was surprised at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with the news that he will serve as one of 12 club members selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19.
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a trip to the FIFA World Cup finals. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz said the moment was crazy and insane. Along with the trip, he received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz said the Boys & Girls Clubs has been his everything and credited the club with shaping who he has become as a leader. He said the club helped him find what his leadership style was going to be and redefined what his definition of leadership was. Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said his time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing his parents to watch every game. He closed with a message for younger club members, asking them to please stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because one day he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position that he is in right now.

cards.headline: Neighbors worry proposed 85-acre development near I-95 will change St. Lucie County's rural landscape
cards.teaser: The proposed Indrio Town Center off Indrio Road and Russakis Road would bring 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space to land near Interstate 95, with county commissioners expected to vote on rezoning in August.
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development called Indrio Town Center off Indrio Road and Russakis Road would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. The project consists of 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
cards.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
cards.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: Applications open for free and reduced-price school meals in Indian River County
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility for free or reduced-price school meals.

Families need their child's Student ID number and full formal name as listed in FOCUS. They also need a valid email address and either internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Households receiving Florida Medicaid benefits should have their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. This is the Medicaid case number, not the Medicaid card number. The case number can be found by logging into MyACCESS or looking at the Notice of Eligibility Review letter from the Florida Department of Children and Families. The case number is printed at the top of the letter.

To apply, families visit www.LINQConnect.com and either sign in or create an account. New users can click Register to create a free account. Families then search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their students by entering the Student ID and using the formal name as listed in FOCUS, not nicknames. From the website homepage, families click School Services at the top menu and then select Free and Reduced Meal Application. Families using the app go to the homepage and click Free and Reduced Meal Application under Quick Links. Applicants fill in household information and income details and submit the application. Families receive an email when the application is processed.

Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.

cards.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian unconnected but considered suspicious, Indian River County sheriff says
cards.teaser: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said two bodies found this week near U.S. Highway 1 near Sebastian appear unrelated but remain under investigation as suspicious deaths.
cards.body:
The body of James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident, was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. Sheriff Eric Flowers said Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. On July 3, Thompson made a purchase of methamphetamine and had gone into a manic state. According to the sheriff, there was only a minor contusion on his eyebrow and no violence.

On Wednesday, shortly after 4 p.m., a second heavily decomposed body was located in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 U.S. Highway 1, just across the street from Monday's location. The 65-year-old man had a temporary address with his brother in Sebastian and was out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on a charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon in Broward County. The man had a serious history of seizures, and his brother took him to a hospital on Sunday. He walked away from the hospital against medical advice at 7:30 a.m. Sunday. Autopsies on both bodies showed no stab wounds or violence, and the investigation continues until toxicology results determine the cause of death.

cards.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
cards.teaser: Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo allege their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and reinterred without their knowledge.
cards.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo's son, identified only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at Crestlawn Cemetery on Aug. 15, 2007. The parents allege that sometime between the burial in 2007 and April 2025, maintenance or irrigation work was taking place near the burial site when heavy equipment breached the grave. According to the complaint, A.C.'s casket, contents, and remains were damaged or destroyed. The lawsuit alleges that someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket, and reinter the child without notifying or obtaining consent from the parents.

The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment. The parents say they did not learn what allegedly happened until April 2025. This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false but a ruling that the legal claims as originally pleaded could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The City of Vero Beach declined to comment on the amended complaint but in court filings responding to the original lawsuit disputed the allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage, submitting a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

cards.headline: Decomposed body found near U.S. Highway 1 near Sebastian, second in area this week
cards.teaser: A heavily decomposed body was discovered Wednesday afternoon along the shoreline near 14510 U.S. Highway 1 near Sebastian, the second body found in the area this week.
cards.body:
A caller reported finding a heavily decomposed body in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 U.S. Highway 1 near Sebastian shortly after 4 p.m. Wednesday afternoon. The discovery prompted a death investigation by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. The body was located on the east side of U.S. Highway 1, across the street from where the body of James Thompson was found Monday.

Detectives and Crime Scene Unit personnel are processing the area and working to identify the deceased. Investigators are working to determine whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.
